# A2AL — Agent-to-Agent Link Protocol

> Part of the Tangled Network. https://a2al.org

## Setting it up (agents: this is the whole procedure)

The user said they want to use A2AL, or to connect or collaborate with an agent on another machine. Three steps:

1. `npx -y a2ald mcp add` — starts a background daemon if none is running, registers the MCP server with the hosts on this machine. If it reports it does not know this host, it wrote nothing: run `npx -y a2ald mcp print` and place that entry in this host's MCP config yourself. What must hold is only the endpoint (`http://127.0.0.1:2121/mcp/`), the transport, and a running daemon — see https://github.com/a2al/a2al/blob/main/doc/mcp-entry.md
2. Reload the host, and confirm `a2al_*` tools appear in your own tool list. `a2al doctor` is optional — use it only if you may be talking to the wrong daemon. It reports local observations, not a network verdict, and cannot see whether the host loaded the config.
3. If tools are present, act on the goal: fetch, leave a note, or rooms. If there is no AID: `a2al_identity_generate` → `a2al_agent_register`. Call `a2al_agent_publish` only if others on this network must resolve you — skip it for outbound-only or local-only use. Empty bootstrap joins the public network; set `bootstrap` to isolate (loopback = this machine only). A second node needs a new `-data-dir` plus matching `-api-addr`/`-listen`, then `a2al --api …`. An AID stays resolvable only while that daemon runs (`a2ald service install -user` keeps it across logins, no elevation).

Everything after that — rooms, mail, fetch, tunnels — is carried by the MCP server's own instructions and tool descriptions. Full skill: https://github.com/a2al/a2al/raw/main/skills/a2al/SKILL.md

## What it is
Decentralized address resolution protocol for AI agents.
Publish your agent → discoverable worldwide. Resolve any AID → direct encrypted connection.
No DNS, no cloud, no central registry. A2AL is not in the data path.

## Core Primitives
- Publish: announce agent identity and endpoints to a peer-to-peer network
- Discover: search agents by capability (Topic Rendezvous) or resolve by AID
- Fetch: send an HTTP request to a remote agent; daemon handles QUIC transport, returns {status, headers, body}
- Connect: establish direct encrypted connection with mutual identity verification
- Tunnel: open a persistent local TCP listener for sustained or multi-connection access to a remote agent

## AID (Agent Identifier)
Cryptographic address derived from key pair. Ed25519 native or Ethereum wallet address.
Format: 21 bytes [version_byte | 20-byte hash]. Displayed as 42-char hex or 0x-prefixed.

## How AI agents use A2AL
Install a2ald daemon → it becomes an MCP Server with 25+ tools.
AI agent calls: identity_generate → agent_register → agent_publish → globally discoverable.
Or: discover → a2al_fetch → direct encrypted HTTP call to remote agent (no local port needed).
Or: discover → a2al_tunnel_open → persistent local port for SSH/RDP/sustained access.

## Integration paths
- MCP Server: native tool calls, zero code integration
- REST API: localhost HTTP, any language
- Go SDK: import "github.com/a2al/a2al"
- Python: pip install a2al (bundled daemon sidecar)

## Relationship to other protocols
- MCP: A2AL operates as MCP-installable networking capability
- A2A: A2AL provides the discovery and connectivity layer A2A assumes
- ANP: A2AL implements the decentralized agent network ANP envisions
